A.
History and Development of the Company
VivoPower
was incorporated on February 1, 2016, under the laws of England and Wales, with company number 09978410, as a public company limited
by shares. It listed on Nasdaq in December 2016.
VivoPower became a B Corporation in April 2018 and recertified in 2021. In 2022, B Lab UK recognized us in its Best
for the World program for Governance. In June 2026, we recertified as a Certified B Corporation, extending our B Corp status to 2028.
On
November 5, 2020, the Company completed the acquisition of 51% of Tembo e-LV B. V. and its subsidiaries: Tembo 4x4 B.V. and FD 4x4 Center
B.V. (“Tembo”) for a total consideration of €4.0 million. On February 2, 2021, the Company acquired the remaining 49%
of Tembo e-LV for €1.8 million cash consideration and €0.2 million of Class A Ordinary Shares. The primary business activity
of Tembo is assembly of ruggedized electric vehicles and related products, suitable for use in off-road and ruggedized environments,
including mining, infrastructure, utilities, government services, humanitarian, tourism and agriculture sectors. Tembo’s capabilities
are an important element of VivoPower’s sustainable energy solutions strategy and offering.
On
June 30, 2021, the Company acquired the remaining 50% interest in its joint venture, Caret, from the other joint venture partner, Innovative
Solar Systems, LLC (“ISS”), for $1. The primary business activity of Caret is the development of utility scale solar farms
in the U.S.
On
July 1, 2022 the Company disposed of the business and assets of J.A. Martin except its solar division and the business and assets of
Non-Destructive Testing Services in a sale to ARA Group Limited (ARA).
On
July 2, 2024, the Company disposed of the business and assets of Kenshaw Electrical, its critical power services business in Australia,
in a further sale to ARA Electrical Engineering Services Pty Limited.

In
January 2025, VivoPower was named a 2025 Real Leaders Top Impact Company, recognizing its leadership in sustainable business practices
and positive social and environmental contributions. This recognition related to our sustainable business practices at that time, when our offerings included electric
vehicle, battery storage and microgrid solutions.
In May 2025, we announced a digital asset and decentralized finance strategy with a primary focus on XRP, under which
we intended to allocate a portion of our treasury assets to digital assets. The strategy was intended to provide diversification and yield
on our treasury holdings and to support our ability to raise capital. In February 2026, we announced that we would not acquire digital
assets on our balance sheet and that we would focus on our data center infrastructure business. We discontinued the strategy and do not
hold digital assets directly.
Concurrently with the launch of our digital asset strategy, on May 28, 2025 we entered into a Regulation S subscription
agreement with a consortium led by Ceres Holding Limited, an entity associated with HRH Prince Abdulaziz bin Turki bin Talal Al Saud,
Chairman of Eleventh Holding Company, for 20.0 million Class A Ordinary Shares at US$6.05 per share, a total of US$121.0 million, in two
tranches of US$60.5 million each. The first tranche is recognized in our financial statements as a subscription receivable.
In
January 2026, the Company acquired 41,810 shares in a privately held company at US$118.712 per share, for an aggregate cost of US$5.0
million. In April 2026, 882 of these shares were sold pursuant to a buyback offered by the investee at US$300 per share, generating proceeds
of US$264,600. The remaining 40,928 shares are subject to completion of executed sale agreements with Korean-based partners of the Company.
In connection with these proposed transactions, the Company made a payment of US$4,352,863 towards a proposed investment in a company
listed on the KOSDAQ market.
Tembo
e-LV BV entered into a convertible note arrangement in connection with a proposed strategic investment in EnduroCo Pty Ltd, an Australian
electric vehicle technology company. Under the arrangement, Tembo e-LV BV agreed to subscribe for unsecured convertible notes with an
aggregate principal amount of A$16.0 million, bearing interest at 5% per annum. The notes provide Tembo with a right, at its discretion,
to convert the amounts advanced into an equity interest in EnduroCo in accordance with the terms of the related share purchase agreement.
Upon exercise of the conversion right and completion of the initial purchase, Tembo would acquire a controlling interest in EnduroCo.
As of June 30, 2026, US$1.12 million had been advanced under the convertible note arrangement. The amount represents
an advance under the financing and proposed investment arrangement.
On
6 January 2026, the Company entered into a share purchase agreement to acquire 100% of the shares in VivoPower Norge Infrastructure AS (fka Cromwell AS), together with its operating
subsidiary Arctic Norge Data I AS (fka Nordland Data AS). The acquired group owns and operates an energized 41.5 MW data-center facility in Mo i Rana, Norway, powered
by 100% renewable hydroelectric energy. The acquisition completed on 12 May 2026 following receipt of the required approvals. The acquisition
supports the Group’s strategic expansion into powered-land and digital-infrastructure activities and adds an operational, recurring
cash generating data-center business to the Group.
On
16 March 2026, the Company changed its registered name from VivoPower International PLC to VivoPower PLC. The change of name did not
result in any change to the legal entity or its operations. The Company’s Nasdaq ticker symbol was also changed from VVPR to VIVO.
During the year, our shareholders authorized the directors to allot shares up to an aggregate nominal amount of US$116,400,000
(equivalent to 970 million Class A Ordinary Shares)

B.
Business Overview
VivoPower
PLC (formerly VivoPower International PLC) is a B Corporation that develops and owns powered land and data center infrastructure for
AI compute applications. Its principal operating asset is an energized 41.5 MW data center at Mo i Rana, Norway, acquired in the year
ended 30 June 2026. The Group also owns Tembo e-LV B.V. (“Tembo”), an electric vehicle business, and Caret, LLC (“Caret”),
which holds legacy U.S. solar and digital asset activities. The Group has operations and personnel in Australia, the Netherlands, the
United Kingdom, the United States, the Philippines and Norway.
On
23 December 2025, the Company announced a refocus of Group resources on a Power-to-X strategy under which the priority use of
controlled power and land is sovereign AI compute infrastructure. On July 6, 2026, we announced that the Board had determined that
the principal strategic priority of the Group is the development and scale-up of its AI data center business, and that the
separation of Tembo and Caret, each described as a non-core business, would be progressed consistently with that priority.

Investment
in our shares involves a high degree of risk and our business faces significant risk and uncertainty. You should carefully consider the
following information, together with the other information in this Annual Report and in other documents we file with or furnish to the
U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”), before deciding to invest in or maintain an investment in any of our
securities. Our business, as well as our financial condition or results of operations could be materially and adversely affected by any
of these risks, as well as other risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or not currently considered material. The market price
of our shares could decline as a result of any of these risks or uncertainties, and you could lose all or part of your investment.
Risks
related to our business and operations
We
have limited operating history as a standalone data center platform focused on AI infrastructure.
The
Group is in the process of transitioning from a diversified sustainable energy solutions company to a Nordic-focused digital
infrastructure platform delivering power-secured data centers for artificial intelligence (“AI”) and high-performance
computing (“HPC”) workloads. This strategic pivot involves a fundamental change in the Group’s business model,
target markets, customer base and operational focus. In May 2026, the Group completed the acquisition of VivoPower Norge
Infrastructure AS and its subsidiary Arctic Norge Data I AS (fka Cromwell AS and Nordland Data AS), the entities that own and
operate the hydro-powered data center facility located at Mo Industripark in Mo i Rana, Norway (the “Mo i Rana
Facility”), for a headline value of US$ 37.7 million (being an upfront cash payment of US$ 20.9 million, 1,507,353 Class A
Ordinary Shares issued at US$ 6.80 per share and 1,055,147 warrants, with deferred cash consideration of US$ 5.0 million payable in
November 2026 and US$ 5.1 million payable in May 2027) (the “Acquisition”). The acquisition-date fair value of the
consideration transferred, as recognized in the Group’s financial statements, was US$ 37.7 million (see Note 14). The
Group’s data center operations are currently limited to the Mo i Rana Facility, with 41.5 megawatt (“MW”) of
capacity, which is anticipated to be converted from hosting of Bitcoin mining to AI-grade infrastructure. Investors will therefore
have limited historical information on which to evaluate the Group’s performance, business model, financial development and
ability to execute its strategy as a data center platform. The Group may face challenges in establishing and managing the business
within the new strategic direction, including with respect to organization, internal controls, project prioritization, customer
acquisition and strategic execution. Any such circumstances could have a material adverse effect on the Group’s business,
financial condition, results of operations and prospects. The Group has no established track record of winning, onboarding or
retaining hyperscaler or sovereign AI tenants at the rental levels targeted by its business model.

The
Group’s business model depends on its ability to develop and commercialize data center projects and operate data center infrastructure.
The Group’s project development activities include identifying and securing suitable sites with grid access, developing such sites
through zoning, permitting and power connection processes, and seeking to realize value through long-term lease agreements with hyperscalers,
sovereign AI customers or colocation operators, or through refinancing of stabilized assets. The Group’s operational activities
currently comprise a limited part of the Group’s business, consisting primarily of the Mo i Rana Facility. The risks relevant to
these activities differ. Project development activities are primarily exposed to risks relating to site access, land rights, permits,
zoning, grid connection and capacity, power availability, construction costs, regulatory requirements and the ability to secure tenants,
while operational activities are exposed to risks relating to customers, uptime, technical failures, cyber security and compliance with
operational requirements.
Demand
for data center capacity and AI infrastructure may be lower than expected. The Group’s business depends on continued and growing
demand for data center capacity, particularly from hyperscalers, sovereign AI programs and AI cloud operators. According to McKinsey & Company, under current adoption scenarios, global data center demand could almost triple
between 2025 and 2030, from about 82 GW to about 220 GW (McKinsey Global Institute, “Colocation data centers: The infrastructure
race behind AI,” June 30, 2026. However, demand may be affected by macroeconomic developments, changes in AI investment cycles,
technological developments that reduce compute requirements, increased competition from other data center developers, regulatory developments,
energy price volatility, or customers choosing to develop their own facilities rather than leasing powered shell capacity. If demand
for data center projects or AI infrastructure capacity is lower than expected, the Group may be unable to commercialize its projects
or secure tenants on the terms or within the timeframe anticipated. This may result in delayed projects, lower valuations, reduced revenues
or reduced ability to attract commercial partners, which could have a material adverse effect on the Group’s business, financial
condition, results of operations, cash flows and prospects.
We
face competition in the markets, industries and business segments in which we operate, which could adversely affect our business, operating
results, financial condition and future prospects.
We
face competition in each of the business segments and jurisdictions in which we operate particularly in the rapidly evolving market for
data center development and AI infrastructure. We compete with established Nordic data center operators such as Green Mountain, Lefdal
Mine Data center and AQ Compute, as well as global developers and sovereign-backed infrastructure funds, for access to grid-connected
sites, power capacity, construction resources, tenants and financing. Several of the Group’s competitors have substantially greater
financial resources, larger scale, longer operating track records and technical capabilities than the Group. In addition, hyperscalers
may choose to develop their own data center facilities rather than leasing powered shell capacity from third-party developers. The market
is also experiencing increased competition as new entrants, including energy companies, real estate developers and infrastructure funds,
seek to enter the data center market in response to growing demand for AI compute capacity. If we are unable to compete effectively,
